utterances.text: When they gave it to me, they told me that it was a decoration for those who played a prominent role in the defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina. It was handed to me by Mr. Ganic, in the presence of Kljujic, Siber, and three or four lower-ranking officers.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: When you say that "they explained to me, they told me," who were you referring to? Who are "they"?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJ PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ganic, the vice-president of the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and Stjepan Kljujic, a member of the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina from the ranks of the Croatian people, and Stjepan Siber, of course, who was the deputy chief of staff of the BiH Army.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Who was the decision-maker for that decoration? Was it the Presidency or some other body?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJ PETKOVIC
utterances.text: They told me that the decoration had been established and awarded by the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Counsel. I apologise if I missed it, but I don't recall and I don't see on the transcript that we ever got a date for this reward. It's come up several times, and it would be nice --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: My next question, my next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since I have to take things at a time, it seemed to me that it was more important to clarify the significance of the decoration and then to deal with the date.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: When was it, General, when you were awarded?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJ PETKOVIC
utterances.text: It was on the 7th of October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: General, which state were you defending at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJ PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Bosnia and Herzegovina. There was no other state.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: In 1993, when you were in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina, which state were you defending at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJ PETKOVIC
utterances.text: There was just one state, Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And in the first half of 1994 when you were in Bosnia and Herzegovina, which state were you defending at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILIVOJ PETKOVIC
utterances.text: Again, the only state in existence was Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Petkovic, earlier on I fully heard the fact that you mentioned that you got the Golden Lily award, and you know that we [as interpreted] obtained it on the 7th of October, 1992, so the date is very clear. But as far as I can recollect, when you are given an award like this, a decree is drafted. And I assume that in a decree to grant you this Golden Lily award, this must have been issued by the president of the Presidency, namely, Mr. Izetbegovic. In this case, did you receive this decree that was published in the "Official Gazette"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't know what they did in terms of administration and paperwork. However, at the end of the meeting they first approached me and the other of my five men. They gave us the Gold Lilies. And they gave one to me to pass on to Mr. Boban, and there was something else with it, a copper pot or something, and I gave the two to Mr. Boban.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but he got another present, as I just told you. It was a hand-made work of craft as a symbol of Bosnia-Herzegovina, or Sarajevo, the famous "Bastacija" [phoen].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. When you are given an award, it is for service rendered, as it were, and what is it that you were awarded it for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, at a meeting held in the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Mr. Ganic thanked the Croatian Defence Council for all that had been done from the month of April 1992 up to then, in terms of the defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina. He particularly emphasised the significance of the operation to liberate the eastern part of Bosnia, or, rather, the eastern bank of the Neretva River, including the town of Stolac. Mr. Ganic apologised for their failure to present the whole situation well to the general public in Bosnia and Herzegovina. To be honest, I held it against him, to a certain extent, but he promised that he would put it right. And then a new meeting with the UNPROFOR was scheduled for the 12th of December, and then Mr. Ganic asked me if he could send me an invitation to that meeting instead of UNPROFOR, and I said, Mr. Kljujic [as interpreted], sure, why not, we will come. And I did come on the 12th of October, and those who had sent me the invitation never turned up. And then I said to General Morillon, Let's go back to the old way of doing things. You send me the invitation.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just a small correction. The first time the date was mentioned, it was the 12th of October, but there is a mistake. Instead of "October ," we have the month of December. Just to avoid confusion.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if we have a bit more time left, we can also talk about December, the next invitation for a meeting in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will have time next week. It is time to close this session. We'll carry on next week and will resume our session Monday at quarter past 2.00. And I thank everyone in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
